q: A student writes: 'Cell respiration produces energy.' Which correction is most accurate?
options: Respiration releases energy from organic compounds and transfers some of it to ATP
Respiration produces energy only when oxygen is present; anaerobic respiration releases none at all
Respiration produces glucose, and that glucose is then converted directly into usable energy
Respiration produces energy from ADP, because ADP is the cell's main long-term energy store
explanation: Energy is converted, never produced (conservation of energy). Respiration releases chemical potential energy stored in organic molecules (glucose, fatty acids, amino acids) and transfers roughly a third of it to ATP; the rest becomes heat. Anaerobic respiration also releases energy (2 ATP per glucose). In exams write 'releases energy' or 'produces ATP' – never 'produces energy'.
